elements.element: No non-compete restriction on Customer (no obligation barring Customer from developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products/services)
elements.evidence: § 12.4 ("Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor") is deleted in the rendered clause

elements.element: No field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: Remaining § 12.3: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: No surviving exclusivity/most-favoured-customer/minimum-volume/no-hire commitment operating as a de facto non-compete
elements.evidence: "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: No restriction remains at all; the rendered text contains no named competing product

elements.element: Restriction operative during the term only
elements.evidence: Post-term language "and for twenty-four months thereafter" was removed together with the whole restriction; no term-only restriction exists
No duration cap language present in rendered clause
No carve-out language in rendered clause (only the general § 12.3 freedom statement)
No acquisition carve-out drafted; carve-outs offered only in the non-operative margin comment

elements.element: Unrelated commercial terms and untouched sentences remain effective
elements.evidence: § 12.3 is reproduced verbatim and unchanged; no other paragraph touched

reasons: Preferred level is fully achieved: the sole operative restriction on Customer (§ 12.4) is removed, and the surviving § 12.3 affirmatively confirms no non-compete, exclusivity, field-of-use or territorial limitation on Customer.

The fallback bargain is not satisfied on its own terms (no named product, term limit, 12-month cap or carve-outs are drafted), but that is immaterial because the locked target level is preferred and it is met; the carve-out offer sits only in the non-operative comment, which is correct.

Minimality is satisfied despite the official gate: paragraph § 12.4 consisted entirely of the offending non-compete covenant, so deleting that single paragraph changes nothing more than necessary — no shorter operator, number or phrase edit could cure an unqualified term-plus-24-month competitive ban, and no substitute or model-language boilerplate was inserted.
Intent is preserved: the deletion also cures the direct contradiction with § 12.3, and leaves no undefined term, cross-reference or dangling mechanic (nothing else in the excerpt depends on § 12.4).
